content:
maria: Repro'd a perf regression on master around the pager + continuous-batching interaction. Long-context requests (~20k tokens) interleaved with short ones cause batch-merge spikes and head-of-line blocking; RSS climbs over a few minutes and KV fragment count keeps increasing.

ajay: Can you paste the minimal logs? wondering if kernel selection changed recently (we picked a newer attention kernel last week).

ben: Quick logs from my run on canary with packed_attention_v2:
```
[run 4790001111] merge_attempt=3 headwait_ms=38 kv_fragments=124 kv_reuse=0 rss_mb=14200
[run 4790001111] merge_attempt=4 headwait_ms=45 kv_fragments=130 kv_reuse=0 rss_mb=14860
```

tess: I uploaded a tiny repro harness and a sampling flamegraph: http://perf/reports/4790001111/flame.svg — flame shows cont-batcher merge thread spinning inside slot_coalesce() and calls into cudaMemAdvise-heavy paths.

maria: Also observed slot_reserved_count growing roughly linearly when longctx sessions are present. Hypothesis: merge policy is greedily merging heads into long tails which forces large page allocations and prevents reuse, causing fragmentation + evictions.

ajay: That matches a kernel-angle: some kernels allocate temporary buffers during merge that blow past our headroom and trigger evict/paging. If kernel selection changed to one with larger temp mem, behavior would amplify.

ben: Quick patch I tried locally: lower prefer_merge_threshold and skip merges when tail is huge. Example pseudo: 
```
if (tail_tokens > 4096 || (tail_tokens / max(1, head_tokens)) > 4) {
  // avoid merging head into a long tail
  skip_merge();
}
```

tess: I added extra debug metrics in the canary build: kv_frag_count, merge_skips, merge_time_ms. Deployed canary-4 at 11:02 — k8sbot: deployment succeeded.

k8sbot: Deployment canary-4 updated: redwood/eng-runtime:canary-kv-debug@sha256:abc123

maria: Plan: collect time series (kv_frag_count, slot_reserved, mem_rss) correlated with batch sizes and kernel hints; run A/B with merge-skip rule and with kernel override to low-mem kernel. Also consider increasing small-prefix TTL to reduce churning.

ben: I'll author a perf job that runs mixed long/short workload (20k, 300, 512 tokens) for 30 minutes and captures frag counts + head_wait hist. Will post results here.

tess: I also added a unit test that simulates continuous-batching merge sequences with interleaved long contexts — test currently fails on master, passes with the merge-skip heuristic.

maria: Good. If merge-skip mitigates the regen we can bisect kernel selection separately. Need to avoid long-term revert; prefer a guarded rollout. :thinking:

ajay: I'll try a two-pronged canary: (A) merge-skip + current kernel, (B) kernel override to mem-friendly + no merge-skip. Compare rss and p50 head_wait after 30m. Posting numbers in ~2h.

ben: FYI logs to look for in traces: 
- "slot_coalesce: merged=... frag_before=... frag_after..."
- "kv_reuse=0" (bad)
- repeated cudaMemAdvise warns

maria: Excellent. Also add a gauge for per-slot fragmentation (fragment_count per slot) — we need that to see whether eviction/paging correlates with specific slot IDs.

ajay: Will do. Thanks all — ping me @maria when you have the perf job output.

ben: Attached perf job id: perf/4790001111-mix-longshort. Will upload graphs when done.

tess: Filed a small issue with repro and suggested patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/1523 — label: eng-runtime/kvcache

maria: Great. If we see quick wins we can roll to canaries this afternoon.
